cards.explanation: The answer is that He gathers them. The psalm says, "He gathers the exiles of Israel." Exiles are people living far from home, and the LORD is the One bringing them in. I know a little about that feeling, friends. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, waiting to be gathered up. The city is built up and the people are gathered, both in the same verse (Psalm 147:2).

The answer is that He heals them. That's the heart of this whole psalm, friends: "He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds." Healing is what the verse says He does. I think a verse that tender is worth reading twice, so go back and read it once more, nice and slow (Psalm 147:3).

The answer is that He calls each one by name. The psalm says, "He determines the number of the stars; He calls them each by name." So He settles the number AND He knows each name. I get a little dizzy thinking about it, because my own sky only has six shapes in it, and each one is one of my cookie cutter kids, with a name I never forget. Think about a sky with every star named (Psalm 147:4).

The answer is True. The psalm says, "Great is our Lord, and mighty in power; His understanding has no limit." No limit at all, not even a little one at the edge. Friends, I can't even keep track of my own mixing bowls, so this one is hard for me to picture (Psalm 147:5).

The answer is humble. "The LORD sustains the humble, but casts the wicked to the ground." The psalm puts two kinds of people side by side, and the humble are the ones He sustains. I can tell you from experience, friends, I was pretty humble in the back of that drawer. Nothing humbles a stamper like a dead battery being the most popular guy in the room (Psalm 147:6).

The answer is with thanksgiving. The psalm says, "Sing to the LORD with thanksgiving…" This is a song with a thank-you inside it. Friends, I've got a LOT to be thankful for, like a gold base, a warm oven and the angel who called me out of a junk drawer. So this one comes easy to me (Psalm 147:7).

The answer is grass. God "…makes grass to grow on the hills." The same passage says He covers the sky with clouds and prepares rain for the earth. Three things God does, and grass is the one in the blank. Hills, I love that (Psalm 147:8).

The answer is the young ravens. He provides food "…for the young ravens when they call." These little ones call out, and the psalm says God provides for them. Jesus points to ravens too, saying they neither sow nor reap, and God feeds them (Luke 12:24). I think that's a pretty good picture of being looked after (Psalm 147:9).

The answer is False. The psalm says, "He does not delight in the strength of the horse; He takes no pleasure in the legs of a man." Both the horse's strength and a man's legs are things He doesn't delight in. Friends, I think that takes a little pressure off, because I will never win a race (Psalm 147:10).

The answer is those who fear Him. The psalm says, "The LORD is pleased with those who fear Him, who hope in His loving devotion." The verse before it listed the horse's strength and a man's legs. Here the psalm turns to the people He is pleased with, and they hope in His loving devotion (Psalm 147:10-11).

The answer is the bars of its gates. The psalm says, "…He strengthens the bars of your gates…" This is the first reason the psalm gives for Jerusalem to praise. A strong gate bar is the kind of thing nobody thinks about until they need it, friends. The psalm says God is the One who strengthens it (Psalm 147:12-13).

The answer is the children within. The psalm says, "…and blesses the children within you." Behind those strong gates, the children are the ones named. I think a verse like that is a happy one, friends. The gate bars are strong, and the little ones inside are blessed (Psalm 147:13).

The answer is peace. The psalm says, "He makes peace at your borders…" The borders are the edges of the land, and the verse says God makes peace there. The same verse goes on to say He fills Jerusalem with the finest wheat. Friends, I'd say that's a good day at the bakery (Psalm 147:14).

The answer is True. The psalm says, "His word runs swiftly." God sends forth His command to the earth, and it goes out at speed. Nobody has to chase it down. You know when you text someone and wait all afternoon for an answer? This is the opposite, and it impresses me (Psalm 147:15).

The answer is hail. The psalm says, "He casts forth His hail like pebbles." It gave us snow like wool and frost like ashes, and now hail like pebbles. Wool, ashes, pebbles, all in a row. Friends, winter shows up in this psalm with a whole set of pictures (Psalm 147:16-17).

The answer is that it melts. The psalm says, "He sends forth His word and melts them…" The snow, frost and hail are all there, and then His word goes out and melts them. The verse goes on to say that when He unleashes His winds, the waters flow. I think that's a pretty good picture of what His word can do (Psalm 147:18).

The answer is Jacob and Israel. The psalm says, "He declares His word to Jacob, His statutes and judgments to Israel." Jacob and Israel are both names the psalm uses here, and God also gave Jacob the name Israel (Genesis 32:28). God declared His word to them (Psalm 147:19).

The answer is False. The psalm says, "He has done this for no other nation; they do not know His judgments." That's what the verse says about the nations, friends. And then the psalm ends the way it began, with "Hallelujah!" (Psalm 147:20).
